decision.reason: 36Kr original 13 October publication specifies a real-world robot skills competition with explicit cross-mode scoring and documented test requirements; a separate manual evidence/score comparison workflow is plausible.

opportunities.core_job: Standardize real-world robot-task scoring across robot form factors and autonomous/teleoperated modes
opportunities.target_customer: Embodied-robot competition organizers and independent pilot evaluation teams
opportunities.product_mechanism: Manual rubric versioning, task result CSV, body type and mode coefficient, reviewer sign-off, source video/evidence link and score comparison
opportunities.why_now: October 23–25 Shanghai 2026 International Embodied Intelligence Skills Competition publishes 9 tracks and 23 real-task assessments with four scoring modules and cross-form factor/mode coefficients.
opportunities.before_state: Different robot forms and teleoperation modes leave task score, execution evidence and assessor judgment in incompatible files
opportunities.after_state: Versioned task rubric → import/manual actual scores → normalize mode coefficients → reviewer evidence and signoff → comparable export
opportunities.source_observation: 36Kr original competition notice confirms 23 events, actual physical scene tests, four scoring modules and autonomous versus teleoperation normalization. This is only a Discovery hypothesis.
